Final cleanup tally (yasyf box, 2026-07-25): **18 leaked test processes across 5 families**, all killed under the gate (pattern + PPID 1 + UID 501), all requiring SIGKILL (every one carries `trap '' TERM`): TestRunCombinedCancellationReapsDaemonizedDescendantAndRecord ×8 (4 parent/child pairs — parents killed first so children reparented to PID 1 and passed the same unmodified gate), TestRuntimeRetainsOwnershipOnIncompleteWorkerSettlement ×4, TestBridgeRecoveryReapsLeaderlessGroupBeforeReceiptAcknowledge ×3, TestProcessVerifierCancellationReapsAndReusesDedicatedLane ×2, TestCmdTransportResetKillsBackgroundedDescendant ×1. Oldest orphan dated Jul 22. Evidence file on the box: /tmp/daemonkit-test-leaks-1785025196.txt, Sections 1-5 (kill sets, temp-dir survey, pre-kill ps lines, lsof proofs, outcomes).

One candidate REFUTED by evidence: PID 13886 (`bash -c while :; do sleep 1; done`) circumstantially matched a killed test's backgrounded subshell, but lsof showed cwd=/Users/yasyf/Code/cookie-sync/internal/daemon, binary /bin/bash (test orphans were all /bin/sh), zero test-dir fds — left running; it belongs to the cookie-sync lineage. Lesson for the record: generic command shapes collide; attribution needs lsof-grade evidence before a kill.

Sharpened framing for whoever claims this: all five leaking families are reaping/cancellation/ownership-settlement tests — the tests proving descendant cleanup are the ones stranding TERM-immune descendants. Investigate whether the gap is in the reap paths under test or in the tests' own teardown when the test binary dies uncleanly (both may be true: teardown never runs on SIGKILL, which is why helpers need parent-death detection of their own).
